submission.natural_language_explanation: N200+ is a layer-5 ' to' pole: its input row is one of only two of the layer's 2048 neurons whose best-aligned vocabulary direction is the unembedding row of ' to' (w_in.W_U ranks ' to' #1 of 50,304, ahead of ' thereto', ' TO', ' unto', ' toward'; the other is its top co-activating partner N689+), so it fires on the token that the model is about to follow with ' to' - the head of a to-infinitive or to-PP complement (want, need, try, able, due, according, related, entitled, response, addition, access, how, order, important, necessary, likely, tend, contributes, rise, proximity). Its strength is graded by the model's own next-token probability of ' to' (mean activation 0.006 where p(' to')<0.2, 0.12 at 0.25, 0.37 at 0.55, 0.82 at 0.85, about 1.0 at 0.95; AUC 0.93 for p(' to')>0.5 and 0.97 for >0.8), so it fires on words the text never follows with ' to' ('the scientists' ability was limited' 1.26) and stays near zero on literal 'X to' that the model does not expect ('learn to', 'go to', 'going to', 'give it to', 'up to' all 0.0-0.2) and on the ' to' token itself (0.00 in every example); its write subtracts about 1 logit from ' to' (it is the layer's strongest ' to' suppressor, z=-15.0) and adds a near-uniform offset elsewhere, while a separate, weaker component fires on token identity alone on word-internal fragments and non-ASCII bytes (' Perm', 'leg', ' le', ' sensit', ' transc', 'र', 'κ', '�') with no ' to' in play.

rival_explanations: A narrower trigger: it fires only where the model's ' to' probability is essentially certain (>=0.9) after a lexical head, and the mid-strength firings ('likely' 0.43 at p=0.84, 'necessary' 1.25 at p=0.61, 'response' 1.33 at p=0.16) are noise, so it should be near zero at any new position where ' to' is merely the leading candidate with p<0.9.

A lexical-bigram detector: it keys on the training-data frequency with which the current word is followed by ' to', so it should also fire on the highest-P(to) predecessors 'going to', 'have to', 'use to', 'learn to' and on dative 'it/them to' wherever they occur, whether or not this model predicts ' to' there.

A general confidence/temperature unit: its write is a near-uniform positive logit offset (it damps entropy at firing positions), so it should fire at any strongly confident position whose top-1 is a common function word, not only where that top-1 is ' to'.

A wide gulf between scientists and reporters is short changing the American public and could have significant societal impact, according to a yearlong joint study by a noted journalist and a senior space scientist.
They found that few scientists have confidence in the media's ability to report science accurately, while most journalists see serious shortcomings in the scientists' ability to describe their work in plain English.
The study was conducted by veteran newsman Jim Hartz and NASA scientist Rick Chappell. During his journalism career, Hartz has frequently chronicled science matters for NBC News and PBS. Chappell is a space physicist who has served as chief scientist for NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Ala., and recently joined Vanderbilt University as director of science and research communications. They undertook the study as visiting professional scholars for The Freedom Forum First Amendment Center at Vanderbilt.
Hartz and Chappell found that the frequent inability of science and the media to communicate effectively with each other seriously undermines science literacy among the general public. This, in turn, creates an electorate ill-prepared to make informed judgments about major issues related to science, health and technology, such as global warming and human cloning, as well as multibillion-dollar federal investments in research and development.
"This study throws fresh sunlight on an issue that's been in the shadows far too long," said Vanderbilt Chancellor Joe B. Wyatt, who provided the impetus for the study.
"Fortunately, there are many positive signs this is one problem that can be fixed, although it will require much attention and work by all parties."
In addition to finding a wide gap between science and the press, the most comprehensive survey to date of scientists and journalists revealed a strong willingness by both sectors to improve the situation. For example, 81 percent of the scientists who responded said they would be willing to take a course to help them learn to better communicate with journalists.
Hartz and Chappell emphasize in their report that public understanding of science leads to support for basic research which, in turn, yields advances that improve the quality of life and strengthen the economy and national security. Without a healthy flow of scientific information, their report says, the United States could lose the material preeminence that was created in large part by the great scientific and technological investments and achievements of the past.
Among the recommendations included in the report are proposals for: journalists to increase their understanding of, and training in, the sciences; the scientific community to train its own members to speak for different scientific disciplines; and science institutions to make research papers and researchers more approachable.

This 77-year-old university librarian lived a quiet, simple life cataloging the school’s media during work days – that’s why the college was all the more shocked when they found out that he had left them a small fortune after his death.
Robert Morin had amassed a $4 million estate which he bequeathed to the University of New Hampshire after he passed away last year.
The donation will go towards scholarships, upgrading the library media room, a video scoreboard for the football field, and a career center for alumni and students alike.
The university explains that Bob was a zealous consumer of media – between 1979 to 1997 he watched more than 22,000 videos. Following this feat, he switched his attention to books. He read, in chronological order, every book published in the U.S. from 1930 to 1940 – excluding children’s books, textbooks and books about cooking and technology. At the time of his death he had reached 1938, the year of his birth.

readings.explanation: N200+ is a layer-5 ' to' pole: its input row is one of only two of the layer's 2048 neurons whose best-aligned vocabulary direction is the unembedding row of ' to' (w_in.W_U ranks ' to' #1 of 50,304, ahead of ' thereto', ' TO', ' unto', ' toward'; the other is its top co-activating partner N689+), so it fires on the token that the model is about to follow with ' to' - the head of a to-infinitive or to-PP complement (want, need, try, able, due, according, related, entitled, response, addition, access, how, order, important, necessary, likely, tend, contributes, rise, proximity). Its strength is graded by the model's own next-token probability of ' to' (mean activation 0.006 where p(' to')<0.2, 0.12 at 0.25, 0.37 at 0.55, 0.82 at 0.85, about 1.0 at 0.95; AUC 0.93 for p(' to')>0.5 and 0.97 for >0.8), so it fires on words the text never follows with ' to' ('the scientists' ability was limited' 1.26) and stays near zero on literal 'X to' that the model does not expect ('learn to', 'go to', 'going to', 'give it to', 'up to' all 0.0-0.2) and on the ' to' token itself (0.00 in every example); its write subtracts about 1 logit from ' to' (it is the layer's strongest ' to' suppressor, z=-15.0) and adds a near-uniform offset elsewhere, while a separate, weaker component fires on token identity alone on word-internal fragments and non-ASCII bytes (' Perm', 'leg', ' le', ' sensit', ' transc', 'र', 'κ', '�') with no ' to' in play.

A narrower trigger: it fires only where the model's ' to' probability is essentially certain (>=0.9) after a lexical head, and the mid-strength firings ('likely' 0.43 at p=0.84, 'necessary' 1.25 at p=0.61, 'response' 1.33 at p=0.16) are noise, so it should be near zero at any new position where ' to' is merely the leading candidate with p<0.9.

A lexical-bigram detector: it keys on the training-data frequency with which the current word is followed by ' to', so it should also fire on the highest-P(to) predecessors 'going to', 'have to', 'use to', 'learn to' and on dative 'it/them to' wherever they occur, whether or not this model predicts ' to' there.

A general confidence/temperature unit: its write is a near-uniform positive logit offset (it damps entropy at firing positions), so it should fire at any strongly confident position whose top-1 is a common function word, not only where that top-1 is ' to'.
